title: DNS failure
symptom: Clients can reach an IP address but hostnames fail to resolve.
inject: On the isolated DHCP router, temporarily configure a deliberately invalid DNS server in the affected pool; renew a lab client lease.
diagnose: ipconfig /all (VPCS) or resolvectl status (Linux client)
show ip dhcp binding and show running-config | section dhcp
nslookup example.com or dig +time=2 example.com
ping <known-reachable-IP> to distinguish name resolution from routing
fix: Correct the DHCP pool dns-server option to the intended resolver, then renew the client lease and clear stale resolver cache if present.
verify: Confirm the client has the intended DNS server; query a known name and test its resolved address.
rollback: Restore the original DHCP pool configuration and renew the client lease.

title: DHCP failure
symptom: A client has no lease or self-assigns an address; other static clients may still communicate.
inject: In the lab only, remove or disable one VLAN's DHCP pool on R1, then release and renew that VLAN's test client.
diagnose: show ip dhcp pool and show ip dhcp binding
show ip interface brief; confirm the VLAN gateway interface is up
show interfaces trunk and show vlan brief
On Linux: sudo tcpdump -ni <interface> 'udp port 67 or udp port 68'
fix: Restore the correct pool network, default-router, exclusions and VLAN scope; ensure DHCP requests reach the router interface or relay.
verify: Renew the client lease; check address, mask, gateway and DNS; ping the gateway.
rollback: Restore the saved startup configuration and return the client to its prior lease state.

title: Duplicate IP address
symptom: Intermittent reachability, changing MAC address in ARP, or duplicate-address warnings.
inject: Use two disposable clients in the same simulated VLAN and assign the same static address; never duplicate an address on a real network.
diagnose: On Linux: ip neigh show; arp -an
On Cisco: show ip arp <address>; show mac address-table dynamic
On Linux client: sudo arping -D -I <interface> <address>
Compare DHCP bindings and both clients' configured addresses
fix: Assign unique addresses or restore DHCP; reserve static addresses outside the dynamic pool and document ownership.
verify: Clear only the lab clients' ARP entries, test repeated gateway and peer pings, and confirm one MAC owns the address.
rollback: Return both lab clients to their recorded unique addresses or DHCP.

title: Packet loss
symptom: Intermittent timeouts and missing replies while the link remains up.
inject: On an isolated Linux lab endpoint only: sudo tc qdisc add dev <lab-interface> root netem loss 25%.
diagnose: ping -c 50 <destination> and compare sent/received/loss
mtr -rw -c 20 <destination> or traceroute -n <destination>
show interfaces <interface> counters/errors on Cisco links
On the injected endpoint: sudo tc qdisc show dev <lab-interface>
fix: Remove the simulated impairment; on real equipment inspect physical errors, duplex/speed, congestion, and each hop to localize loss.
verify: Delete the lab qdisc and repeat the same packet count; confirm loss returns to baseline.
rollback: sudo tc qdisc del dev <lab-interface> root (isolated lab interface only).

title: High latency
symptom: Connections work but response time is consistently above baseline.
inject: On an isolated Linux lab endpoint only: sudo tc qdisc add dev <lab-interface> root netem delay 300ms.
diagnose: ping -c 20 <destination> and compare RTT min/avg/max with baseline
mtr -rw -c 20 <destination> to find where RTT increases
Check interface utilization, drops, errors and route changes
Compare DNS lookup time with direct-IP TCP connect time
fix: Remove the lab delay; for real incidents isolate the high-delay hop and investigate congestion, path changes, shaping or overloaded devices.
verify: Repeat measurements after removing impairment and compare against the saved baseline.
rollback: sudo tc qdisc del dev <lab-interface> root (isolated lab interface only).

title: VLAN misconfiguration
symptom: A host receives the wrong subnet or cannot reach its VLAN gateway while the physical link is up.
inject: On the lab switch, place one test access port in the wrong VLAN or remove its VLAN from the router trunk allowed list.
diagnose: show vlan brief and show interfaces <port> switchport
show interfaces trunk; compare allowed and native VLANs at both ends
show ip interface brief on R1; inspect the matching dot1Q subinterface
Check client address/mask and ARP entry for the expected gateway
fix: Set the access port to the intended VLAN and ensure that VLAN is active and permitted on the trunk; match router subinterface encapsulation.
verify: Renew the client lease; confirm the expected subnet, gateway ARP and reachability.
rollback: Restore the saved port and trunk configuration.

title: Routing failure
symptom: Local subnet works but remote subnets are unreachable; route or OSPF adjacency is missing.
inject: In the lab only, shut one R1-R2 OSPF link or remove its OSPF network statement.
diagnose: show ip ospf neighbor and show ip ospf interface brief
show ip route and show ip route ospf
show ip interface brief; verify link state and /30 addressing
ping the directly connected next hop, then trace toward the remote subnet
fix: Restore the interface/network statement; match OSPF area, timers, subnet, authentication and passive-interface policy at both ends.
verify: Confirm adjacency reaches FULL and the expected remote route is installed; test end-to-end traffic.
rollback: Restore the saved OSPF and interface configuration; compare running config with startup config.

title: Network outage
symptom: Multiple users or VLANs lose connectivity at the same time.
inject: In the lab only, shut the R1 uplink or the sole trunk of one access switch to simulate a shared failure point.
diagnose: Determine blast radius by VLAN, site and service; check monitoring timestamps
show interfaces status; show ip interface brief; inspect link LEDs/state
Check switch trunks, spanning-tree state and router adjacencies
Use ping and traceroute from nearest unaffected and affected points
fix: Restore the failed interface/trunk or replace the failed lab link; for real incidents follow change control and failover procedures.
verify: Validate link, route convergence, DHCP and service reachability from affected segments; monitor stability.
rollback: Return the injected lab link/state to baseline and confirm no unintended config remains.

title: TCP connection failure
symptom: Name resolution and IP reachability work, but a specific TCP service cannot be established.
inject: In the lab, stop the test server or use a deliberately closed destination port; leave routing and firewall unchanged.
diagnose: getent hosts <name> or nslookup <name>
ping <address> (supporting evidence only; ICMP does not prove TCP service health)
nc -vz -w 3 <address> <port> or curl -v telnet://<address>:<port>
On server: ss -lntp; verify service bind address and logs
fix: Start the service and bind it to the intended interface/port; correct the client destination or server configuration.
verify: Confirm a listening socket and successful TCP handshake from the client; test the application response.
rollback: Stop the temporary lab service or restore the server's recorded configuration.

title: Firewall blocking traffic
symptom: The service listens and routes exist, but connection attempts time out or are rejected only across a policy boundary.
inject: In the lab only, add a narrow deny rule for the test source/destination/port to the Guest ACL or isolated namespace firewall.
diagnose: Confirm source, destination, protocol and port with ss/nc or tcpdump
show access-lists and inspect hit counters on the Cisco lab router
On Linux lab firewall: sudo nft list ruleset; inspect counters and chain policy
Compare the failing path with an allowed source and check return-path rules
fix: Adjust the specific lab rule to allow only the required source, destination and service; preserve default-deny policy where intended.
verify: Retest the TCP service and inspect counters/logging; verify unrelated traffic remains restricted.
rollback: Restore the saved ACL/ruleset or remove the exact temporary rule; never flush a production firewall.
